resources.string: An e-ink look for your OLED screen
On — the screen refreshes like paper
Turn on the PaperScreen accessibility service to use PaperScreen.
Refresh only when the screen changes
Skips the page-turn while nothing on screen is moving. Turn off to refresh on every interval.
Applies the current filter to this screen while held.

PaperScreen draws its filtered screen as an accessibility overlay. That\'s the only kind of overlay Android lets be fully opaque while your taps still reach the apps underneath. PaperScreen doesn\'t read anything on your screen through this service.\n\nOn the next screen, open Installed apps (or Downloaded apps), choose PaperScreen, and turn it on. Then come back here.
\n\nIf the switch is greyed out as a \"restricted setting\", open App info for PaperScreen, tap ⋮ in the top corner, choose \"Allow restricted settings\", and try again.
Screen capture permission is needed to run PaperScreen.
Couldn\'t start PaperScreen. Make sure its accessibility service is still on, then try again.
Shows your screen in e-ink style

PaperScreen redraws your screen in the style of an e-ink display, with a paper-like grey page turn on each refresh. It uses this service only to draw a full-screen overlay that your taps pass through. It doesn\'t read or change anything on your screen through this service. Screen capture is asked for separately, each time you turn PaperScreen on.
Shown while PaperScreen is filtering your screen.
Refreshes on change, at most every %1$d ms · tap to adjust
Paused while the screen is off or locked
